messages:
maria: Heads-up — after the RBAC policy push to tighten keystore access in apac this morning, we're seeing intermittent mTLS handshake failures between ingest-proxy and model-runtime. Happening ~1 every 30s for a short burst. Anyone tracking?
kevin: I have logs from the proxy. Pattern is client cert auth failing. excerpt: ```TLS handshake error: tls: bad certificate\nremote_addr=10.12.5.3:52344 service=model-runtime route=/v1/generate``` Looks like client cert presented but rejected.
sam: Did we also change KMS key policy? cert-rotator needs kms:Decrypt on the key-alias to unwrap CSR certs. If RBAC removed the role that rotator uses, it will keep renewing with a cert that doesn't map to a valid identity.
kevin: Checking KMS logs now, seeing several Deny events for kms:Decrypt to role arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/cert-rotator-apac. Example: "ERROR KMS Deny - Requester=cert-rotator-apac Action=Decrypt KeyId=alias/apac-keystore"
asha: If cert-rotator can't unwrap the private key, it might issue a cert chain that doesn't include the expected intermediate, or the client identity won't match the CN/SAN mapping we enforce in proxy RBAC. Also check OCSP stapling — if stapling fails the proxy can reject.
maria: audit-bot, can you surface who applied the RBAC change and show the policy diff? We need to know whether role binding was removed or just permission narrowing.
audit-bot: AUDIT: 4076543208 RBAC_UPDATE user=kevin action=modify_resource resource=apac/keystore permissions_removed=[iam:PassRole,kms:Decrypt] diff_link=https://audit.redwood/patch/6543
kevin: That explains it. I approved a tighter policy (my bad) but didn't realize cert-rotator relies on kms:Decrypt. Rolling back a tiny bit to restore kms:Decrypt for cert-rotator role now.
deploy-bot: canary rollback started for cert-rotator-apac at 4076543780. Monitoring health checks.
maria: Good. While rollback runs: list of immediate checks — 1) verify KMS decrypt Allow for cert-rotator role; 2) check cert serials on model-runtime and proxy to ensure newly minted certs aren't stuck; 3) check ocsp/responder reachability; 4) confirm proxy RBAC mapping still valid.
sam: Also validate keystore rotation didn't create a stale alias mapping. I recommend running: ```aws kms list-keys --region ap-northeast-1``` and confirm alias mapping for alias/apac-keystore -> KeyId match expected.
kevin: After rollback we see KMS Decrypt allow events and handshake failures drop to zero. logs: "KMS Decrypt allowed for cert-rotator-apac" then "TLS handshake success"
maria: Phew. Two follow-ups: 1) update RBAC change playbook to include a cert-rotator and KMS dependency checklist before applying; 2) add an alert rule that flags KMS Deny events for keys that are owned by cert systems (high severity).
asha: Also propose an automated preflight: simulate a cert refresh on a canary service after RBAC changes that touch keystore or kms policies. If the canary fails to unwrap, block rollout.
kevin: Filed INC-1234 for the incident record and included timeline + logs. I'll add the exact policy diff and my rollforward/rollback notes.
maria: Thanks. Assigning owners: kevin for policy doc + rollback notes, asha for playbook update + canary test, sam for alerting rule and KMS log dashboards. We'll do a postmortem tomorrow 0900 PT. :thumbsup:
